newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Klima rules out Austrian NATO entry in first round.
newsitem.headline: Klima rules out Austrian NATO entry in first round.

text.p: Austrian Chancellor Viktor Klima said on Friday there was no question of Austria joining NATO in the first round of its expansion, expected to include former Warsaw Pact states.
"This expansion is for former eastern bloc states," Klima said in an interview with Die Kurier newspaper. "Austria was not and is not an eastern bloc country."
A NATO summit in Madrid in July is expected to name Poland, Hungary, the Czech Republic, and possibly Slovenia, as candidates for membership of the western defence alliance by 1999.
"A neutral country that is a member of the European Union (EU) and makes its own decisions about joining NATO would be accepted any time. It does not need any package," Klima said.

He said his Social Democrat party, which rules in coalition with the conservative People's Party, had pledged to analyse the development of common security structures within the EU, but ruled out joining an existing military pact at this time.
People's Party leader and Foreign Minister Wolfgang Schuessel caused a political stir in Brussels last month when he openly stated that he supported Austria's early entry to NATO.

Quizzed in parliament this week over his comments, Schuessel said he was speaking as a conservative politician and not as foreign minister. He insisted the government was still speaking with one voice over NATO.
Austria, straddling the former Cold War border between Europe's East and West blocs, has been neutral since 1955, when it drew up its post-World War Two constitution.

The Soviet Union, which occupied Austria after the war with allies Britain, France and the United States, demanded that Austria enshrine neutrality in its national charter before it agreed to withdraw its troops.
